D1.bug: When the scan queued older candidates in to_remove and a later comparison set drop_new=True, the scan broke and the branch that APPLIES to_remove never ran, yet those never-applied IDs were still returned and counted in state.redundancy_removals and in the accept event's details['removed'].
D1.fail_before_evidence: tests/test_stage3b_followup_repair_d1.py: 3 failed, 7 passed. Concrete red output: `AssertionError: D1: accept event reported [3, 9] but only the newcomer was actually deleted` and `assert [3, 9] == [9]`.
D1.fix: Build the ledger only from removals that actually shrank the candidate list, using CandidateSet.remove's boolean return. Deletion order, pair-search order, tie-breaking and promotions are unchanged.
D1.pass_after_evidence: Same 19 repair tests pass (D1 10 + D2 9); full suite 302 passed.

D2.bug: All events were accumulated into the cumulative counters BEFORE the checkpoint loop, so every prefix checkpoint (including arrival 100) reported end-of-run totals.
D2.fail_before_evidence: tests/test_stage3b_followup_repair_d2.py: 4 failed, 5 passed. Concrete red output: `AssertionError: D2: checkpoint 100 still equals the final total` / `assert 400 != 400`.
D2.fix: Consume events chronologically and snapshot counters at each checkpoint's own prefix. A pool_flush is not an arrival; the post-stream final flush is counted only in the terminal summary.
D2.pass_after_evidence: Same 19 repair tests pass; full suite 302 passed.

invariance_proof: 50/50 ARCENE runs reproduce the saved Stage 3B ordered selected IDs and arrival positions exactly, proving the repairs are diagnostic-only.
